turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Describe a frontend feature you worked on. How did data move from a user action to the interface, and what did you implement?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: My name is Maya Chen. I built the queue filters in React. Changing a filter updated URL parameters, triggered a request to the existing API, and put the returned rows into local state. I used an increasing request number so an older response could not replace the newest rows. I did not build the API or the shared table.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through a user-facing defect you investigated. What did you observe, and how did you decide what was causing it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I reproduced a stale queue by delaying one request in the browser. The network panel showed the second response arriving first, then the first response replacing its rows. I logged the request numbers alongside each state update; that linked the overwrite to response order rather than to cached data.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you check the change and decide it was ready for release?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I wrote a test with two deferred mocked requests. I resolved the newer one first and asserted that its rows stayed visible after resolving the older one. I also checked that an error response removed the loading indicator. I did not test against the real backend.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What accessibility work or checks did you perform on this interface?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I associated the filter label with its select element and used Tab and Shift+Tab to reach and leave it. I checked that the visible focus indicator stayed on the active control. I did not use a screen reader.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Looking back, what were the limits of your ownership or evidence, and what would you investigate or ask for help with next?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Another engineer reviewed my changes. We had not deployed them when I left the project, so I cannot claim a production improvement. I would next verify real API timing and screen-reader announcements.
